findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate datetime-keyed querysets used by audit logs
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key (line 838-840) and value_from_cursor (842-843) are numeric-only: get_item_key does `int(math.floor(value) ...)` on the attribute named by the order_by key, and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor value. The new audit-log endpoint instantiates this paginator with order_by="-datetime", where AuditLogEntry.datetime is a DateTimeField. On the very first page (after fetching rows) `build_cursor` calls `get_item_key(results[-1])`, and `math.floor()` on a `datetime` raises `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime`, producing a 500. Even if that were fixed, value_from_cursor returning an int would be fed into `build_queryset`'s WHERE clause as the datetime value, so subsequent pages would filter incorrectly or error in Postgres. This paginator should extend DateTimePaginator (which formats/parses datetimes) rather than duplicating Paginator's numeric handling. As written, every request that reaches the optimized path crashes.

findings.title: Negative-offset 'advanced' branch passes a negative slice to Django and raises
findings.body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, when enable_advanced_features is set and cursor.offset < 0, the code does `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` with start_offset = cursor.offset (negative). Django QuerySets do not support negative slicing; `QuerySet.__getitem__` raises `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported` (ValueError in some versions) for a negative slice start. The comment claims 'the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically', which is false. A client can craft a cursor like `value:-1:0` (Cursor.from_string accepts negative offsets), triggering a 500 for anyone who reaches this code path. The negative-offset feature is therefore non-functional and provides a way to crash the endpoint.

findings.title: Possible AttributeError on organization_context.member when it is None
findings.body: `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` dereferences `organization_context.member` without a None check. RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is optional (None when no org membership mapping is present, which can happen on control-silo endpoints). When the user is not a superuser and member is None, this line raises AttributeError and 500s instead of falling back to the standard paginator. Guard with `organization_context.member and organization_context.member.has_global_access` or use the member-access helpers.

findings.title: BasePaginator 'negative offset' change is a no-op and the comment misdescribes behavior
findings.body: The new `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` is behavior-identical to the previous `queryset[offset:stop]` for all non-negative offsets, and for is_prev it keeps offset unchanged, so it does not enable 'bidirectional pagination without full dataset scanning' as the comment claims. For a negative non-prev offset it only changes behavior by silently clamping to 0 (previously the negative slice errored) rather than improving performance. The comment is misleading about both the purpose and the safety of the change; the underlying Django ORM does not support negative offsets, so they are neither efficient nor safe.

findings.title: Cursor comment claims negative offsets are allowed but code is unchanged
findings.body: The added comment says 'Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination scenarios', but `self.offset = int(offset)` is exactly the original line and performs no validation or special handling. Cursor offsets have always been able to be negative (from_string parses arbitrary ints); the comment implies a new capability that does not exist and contradicts the actual negative-offset handling elsewhere. It should be removed or reworded to describe real behavior.

findings.title: No tests for the new OptimizedCursorPaginator or the optimized endpoint branch
findings.body: The PR adds a new paginator class and a request-controlled branch in OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint (including an authorization check and a negative-offset code path) with no unit or endpoint tests. Given that the datetime-key mismatch and negative-offset crash above would be caught by even a single test exercising optimize_pagination=true on the audit-log endpoint, the absence of tests means these regressions ship undetected. Add tests covering the optimized path with datetime ordering, the permission gate, and crafted negative-offset cursors.
